caption: why does the bell ring when I open my window 🔔
logline: Every time a Saltmouth kid opens his bedroom window, the village bell outside rings and the whole village runs indoors; he's sure the bell likes him, and tonight he climbs out past it to wave hi to the pale guy on the cliff.
question: why does the bell ring every time he opens his window?
premise: For three hundred nights, every time the kid opens his upstairs window, the village bell right outside it rings and the whole village runs inside. It only rings for his window, so he's sure the bell likes him and the villagers are shy. Mom: 'Shutters SHUT, honey' (he thinks she's afraid he'll catch a cold). Up on the cliff, under the old oak, there's a super pale guy who never leaves the shade. And once the bell had a little feather sticking out of it, then poof, gone. Tonight the bell rings again and he climbs out past it to wave hi.
twist: Nobody rings the bell. A skeleton lives in the shade of the oak on the cliff (skeletons shelter from the sun) and shoots at the only player in the village whenever he shows himself: the kid at his open window. The bell hangs on the arrow's line between the oak and his window, so every arrow hits the bell (vanilla: a projectile rings a bell; a rung bell sends villagers indoors). The bell was a shield. Tonight he climbs out past it to wave hi, and the skeleton draws on him with nothing in between. Cut on the draw.
